subsystems.name: Reactor pressure vessel
subsystems.role: holds the simulated vent fluid at the pressure and temperature of the seafloor, tens of metres down.

subsystems.name: Gradient chamber
subsystems.role: brings an alkaline, hydrogen-rich fluid into contact with an acidic, CO2-rich fluid without letting them simply mix.

subsystems.name: Mineral membrane
subsystems.role: the catalytic barrier itself — iron-sulphide and nickel-iron-sulphide precipitates that form when the two fluids meet and separate them into compartments.

subsystems.name: Feed and gas supply
subsystems.role: delivers H2, CO2 and dissolved metals in controlled ratios.

subsystems.name: Analysis
subsystems.role: finds out which organic molecules, and how many, the reactor made.

subsystems.name: Sampling and quench
subsystems.role: pulls fluid out of a hot, pressurised cell without letting the products degrade.

buildSteps.title: Choose the vent analogue
buildSteps.detail: Set fluid chemistry from a real alkaline system such as the Lost City field, discovered in 2000: warm (roughly 40–90 °C), alkaline, hydrogen-rich water percolating through iron-bearing rock.

buildSteps.title: Design the mixing geometry
buildSteps.detail: Work out how two fluids at several pH units apart can meet across a thin precipitate without turbulent mixing washing the gradient away.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the cell
buildSteps.detail: Machine the pressure vessel and cut the microfluidic or porous network that defines where the mineral barrier will sit.

buildSteps.title: Establish the gradient
buildSteps.detail: Pump the alkaline and acidic feeds at matched rates; the pH difference and the iron-sulphide precipitation do the rest, building the barrier in place.

buildSteps.title: Add carbon and energy sources
buildSteps.detail: Feed dissolved CO2 and H2 with nickel, iron and sulphur species so the fresh mineral surfaces can catalyse carbon fixation.

buildSteps.title: Run and log
buildSteps.detail: Hold the cell at vent conditions for hours to days, tracking pH, redox and temperature along its length.

buildSteps.title: Quench and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Sample the outflow under pressure, cool it and search for formate, acetate, methane and phosphorylated compounds.

buildSteps.title: Test the membrane's electrical behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Measure whether the mineral barrier sustains a proton gradient comparable to the one living cells maintain across their membranes.

prerequisites.why: the reactor is only as good as the field measurements of real alkaline vent fluids it copies.
gradients across thin mineral layers exist only if flow can be controlled at small scale under pressure.
iron-sulphide and nickel-sulphide surfaces are known to make small organics, but yields and selectivity remain limited.
energy-rich compounds such as acetyl phosphate can phosphorylate organics without enzymes, but the link to a working metabolism is unproven.

prerequisites.tech: A testable theory of the first metabolism
prerequisites.why: the hypothesis that proton gradients across inorganic membranes drove the earliest carbon fixation is coherent but not yet demonstrated end to end.

pathway.milestone: bench reactors demonstrably make organic molecules and sustain a proton gradient across a self-assembled iron-sulphide membrane
pathway.unlocks: a physically plausible energy source for the first metabolism.

pathway.milestone: autocatalytic, self-sustaining carbon fixation in the reactor, producing its own catalysts and energy currency
pathway.unlocks: chemistry that no longer needs a biologist feeding it.

pathway.milestone: coupling that chemistry to simple compartmentalised replicators
pathway.unlocks: a bridge from protometabolism towards the earliest cells.

pathway.milestone: either a general account of how metabolism began, or a demonstration that it did not begin this way
pathway.unlocks: a decisive answer to where life came from — and, incidentally, a toolkit for making chemicals under mild conditions without enzymes.
